pages.text: Saturn's largest moon is the only other world we know with rain, rivers, lakes and seas on its surface - of methane, at 94 K, under an air half again as thick as Earth's. Reach it with a $(item)Cryogenic Lander$() (research $(thing)Titan$()): stand under open sky in the Overworld and use it. Used again on Titan, it lifts off and brings you home under its parachute.

It has six regions. $(thing)Kraken Mare$(), a sea of liquid methane over a floor of tholin sand. The $(thing)Shangri-La Dunes$(), tholin piled by the wind. The $(thing)Xanadu Uplands$(), bare water-ice bedrock. The $(thing)Ontario Lacus Basin$(), lakes and the bright crust of lakes that have dried up. The $(thing)Sotra Cryovolcanic Field$(), where cryolava - ammonia and water - wells up from below. And $(thing)Selk$(), a plain pocked with impact craters, each a bowl with a raised rim, the big ones with a peak in the middle.

Under everything lies the $(item)Subsurface Seal$(): ice VI, crushed denser than water by the ice above it. Titan's hidden ocean is beneath it, and nothing yet made can get through. Falling out of the bottom of Titan sends you home.

Titan's rock is $(item)Water-Ice Bedrock$(): electrolysed, it gives $(fluid)Oxygen$(). $(item)Tholin Sand$() gives up its $(item)Tholin$() to methanol in the Chemical Reactor, and tholin boiled with water gives $(item)Amino Acids$() - the haze makes the building blocks of life out of methane and sunlight. The haze is so thick that from the ground you cannot see Saturn at all.
